This Privacy Policy explains how Jibly collects, uses, shares, stores and protects personal data when you use the Jibly platform at jibly.io, create or manage an Account, post an Item Request or Trip, make or accept a Booking, communicate with other Users, make or receive payments, complete identity verification, submit a review or contact us for support.

Jibly operates an online peer-to-peer marketplace that connects Senders with Travellers who are willing to carry eligible Items during journeys they are already making. In providing the Platform, we process personal data relating to Senders, Travellers, Recipients and other individuals who interact with Jibly or are involved in a Booking.

This Privacy Policy applies to personal data for which Jibly determines the purposes and means of processing. In some parts of the Platform, third-party service providers such as Stripe may process personal data under their own terms and privacy notices, including for payment processing, payouts and identity verification. Where this happens, their handling of personal data may be governed separately by their own privacy practices.

This Privacy Policy should be read together with Jibly’s Marketplace Terms and any other privacy or data protection notices we provide when collecting particular information. It is intended to explain what information we collect, why we use it, who we may share it with, how long we keep it and the rights available to you under applicable data protection law.

By using the Platform, you acknowledge that your personal data will be handled as described in this Privacy Policy. Where we rely on consent for a particular use of personal data, we will ask for that consent separately where required by law.

Please read this Privacy Policy carefully before providing personal information to us or using Jibly. If you have any questions about this Privacy Policy, how we handle your personal information or wish to exercise a data protection right, you can contact us at contact@jibly.io.
INFORMATION WE COLLECT
We collect different types of personal data depending on how you use Jibly, the information you choose to provide and the features or services involved. This may include:
Account and profile information

, such as your name, email address, telephone number, city, country, profile photograph, Account status and verification status. Passwords are handled through our authentication provider and are not stored by Jibly in readable form.
Identity verification information

, such as verification status, verification timestamps and related reference information received through Stripe Identity. Identity documents, selfies and other verification materials are submitted directly to Stripe and are not stored by Jibly as copies of the underlying documents or images.
Booking, Item and Trip information

, including collection and delivery locations, dates, Item category, title and description, weight, dimensions where provided, photographs, Item declarations, Recipient details, departure and destination information, flight or journey details where provided, carrying capacity, accepted Item categories, Offers, matches, Traveller Compensation and Booking status.
Payment and payout information

, including transaction amounts, payment status, refunds, chargebacks, payout status and Stripe transaction or account references. Full payment card details and bank account details are generally collected and processed directly by Stripe rather than stored by Jibly.
Handover and delivery information
, including Handover Codes, Delivery Codes, confirmation timestamps, delivery photographs where uploaded and other information used to verify collection, delivery or attempted delivery of an Item.
Communications and submitted content

, including messages exchanged through the Platform, communications with Jibly, support requests, complaints, dispute information, photographs, descriptions and other content submitted through the Platform.
Reviews and marketplace activity
, including ratings, reviews, listings, Offers, Booking history, cancellations, no-shows, disputes and other activity connected with your Account.
Technical and usage information

, such as IP address, browser type, device information, operating system, access times, session information, pages or features used, security logs and similar technical data generated when you use the Platform.
Safety, fraud and compliance information

, including information relating to suspected fraud, prohibited activity, payment disputes, chargebacks, Account restrictions, complaints, legal requests and investigations into misuse of the Platform.
Information generated by Jibly

, such as Account status, verification status, Booking status, cancellation history, dispute outcomes, fraud indicators, security records and internal administrative records created through your use of the Platform.

We may also receive personal data from other Users and from third-party service providers. For example, a Sender may provide the name or contact details of a Recipient, another User may provide information about you during a dispute, or Stripe may provide us with verification, payment or transaction information.

If you provide personal data relating to another person, you must ensure that you are entitled to provide that information and, where appropriate, that the person has been informed about how their information may be used.

You should not provide sensitive personal data, identity documents, financial information or other information that Jibly has not requested unless it is reasonably necessary for a specific Platform function or Jibly has asked you to provide it. Jibly may remove, restrict or decline to retain information that is unnecessary, inappropriate or submitted contrary to the Marketplace Terms.

We aim to collect only personal data that is reasonably necessary for the purposes described in this Privacy Policy, although the categories of information we collect may change as the Platform, its features or legal requirements develop.
IDENTITY VERIFICATION

Jibly requires identity verification for certain Platform activities, including before a Sender can make a payment and before a Traveller can publish a Trip. Identity verification is carried out through Stripe Identity or another verification provider that Jibly may use from time to time.

As part of the verification process, you may be asked to provide an identity document, photograph, selfie or other information required to confirm your identity. This information is submitted directly to the verification provider and is processed in accordance with that provider’s own privacy practices. Jibly does not ordinarily receive or store copies of your underlying identity documents, selfies or other verification images.

Jibly may receive limited information from the verification provider, such as whether verification was successful, the status and date of the verification, relevant reference identifiers and information reasonably necessary to operate, secure or administer your Account.

We use identity verification information to confirm eligibility to use relevant Platform features, reduce fraud and impersonation, protect Users, support payment and payout processes, investigate misuse and comply with legal or regulatory requirements where applicable.

Verification does not amount to an endorsement, guarantee or representation by Jibly as to a User’s reliability, conduct or suitability. Jibly may require a User to complete, repeat or update verification where reasonably necessary, including where information appears inaccurate, verification expires, an Account is changed or there are security, fraud or compliance concerns.
LEGAL BASIS FOR PROCESSING YOUR INFORMATION

We only process personal data where we have a lawful basis for doing so. The lawful basis that applies will depend on the particular information involved and the reason we are processing it. Under applicable data protection law, Jibly may rely on one or more of the following lawful bases:
Performance of a contract

– where processing is necessary to provide the Platform, administer your Account, facilitate a Booking, process a transaction, enable communications or otherwise perform our obligations under the Marketplace Terms, or to take steps at your request before entering into a contract.
Legitimate interests

– where processing is necessary for Jibly’s legitimate business interests or those of another person, provided those interests are not overridden by your rights and freedoms. This may include protecting the Platform and its Users, preventing fraud and misuse, maintaining security, administering disputes, improving our services, keeping appropriate business records and establishing, exercising or defending legal claims.
Legal obligations

– where processing is necessary for Jibly to comply with a legal or regulatory obligation that applies to us, including obligations relating to tax, accounting, regulatory requests, court orders, law-enforcement requests or other requirements imposed by law.
Consent

– where we ask you to give specific consent for a particular use of your personal data. Where we rely on consent, you may withdraw it at any time, although this will not affect the lawfulness of processing carried out before withdrawal.
Recognised legitimate interests

, where available under applicable UK data protection law, where processing is necessary for a purpose specifically recognised by law, such as certain activities relating to crime prevention, safeguarding or responding to emergencies.
In limited circumstances, we may also process personal data where necessary to protect the vital interests of you or another person.

Different lawful bases may apply to different processing activities, and in some cases more than one lawful basis may be relevant. We identify the appropriate basis by considering the nature of the processing, why it is necessary and our relationship with the individual concerned.
Where we process special category personal data or information relating to criminal offences, we will only do so where an additional condition required by applicable data protection law is satisfied.
HOW WE USE YOUR INFORMATION
We may use your personal data for the following purposes:
To create and manage your Account
, including registration, authentication, profile management, verification status and general Account administration.
To operate the Jibly marketplace
, including publishing Item Requests and Trips, displaying relevant information to other Users, facilitating matches, Offers and Bookings, and administering marketplace activity.
To facilitate payments and payouts
, including processing Payments, Traveller Compensation, Jibly Fees, refunds, reversals, chargebacks and Payouts through Stripe, and maintaining appropriate transaction records.
To verify identity and eligibility
, including confirming whether a User has completed required identity verification and whether they are eligible to access particular Platform features.
To facilitate handover and delivery
, including generating and recording Handover Codes and Delivery Codes, recording confirmation events, and supporting proof of collection, delivery or attempted delivery.
To enable communications between Users
, including in-Platform messaging and communications relating to a Booking, Trip, Item Request, handover, delivery or dispute.
To provide customer support
, including responding to questions, complaints, technical issues, refund requests and other enquiries.
To manage cancellations, disputes and claims
, including reviewing Booking information, messages, photographs, codes, timestamps, payment records and other relevant evidence in order to determine Platform or payment outcomes.
To protect Users and the Platform
, including detecting, preventing and investigating fraud, impersonation, prohibited activity, payment abuse, suspicious behaviour, security incidents and breaches of the Marketplace Terms.
To enforce our agreements and policies
, including investigating suspected misuse, restricting or suspending Accounts and taking steps in relation to unpaid amounts, chargebacks, off-platform circumvention or other prohibited conduct.
To provide ratings and reviews functionality
, including publishing, administering and moderating ratings and reviews and investigating content reported as abusive, misleading, fraudulent, unlawful or otherwise inappropriate.
To communicate with you about the Platform

, including sending Account confirmations, Booking updates, payment and payout notifications, security alerts, handover or delivery information, support communications and important notices about our services, policies or legal terms.
To maintain and improve Jibly
, including troubleshooting, testing functionality, monitoring performance, analysing how Platform features are used, improving user experience and developing or refining our services.
To maintain security and technical integrity
, including monitoring systems, detecting unauthorised access, maintaining logs, protecting Accounts and preventing abuse of our infrastructure.
To maintain appropriate business and legal records
, including transaction, support, dispute, accounting, compliance and administrative records.
To comply with applicable law and regulatory requirements
, including responding to lawful requests, court orders or regulatory enquiries and meeting applicable legal, tax, accounting or reporting obligations.
To establish, exercise or defend legal rights
, including in connection with complaints, disputes, claims, investigations or legal proceedings.
To prevent and investigate misuse of the Platform

, including prohibited Items, false information, duplicate or abusive Accounts, dishonest chargebacks, manipulation of reviews, misuse of payment functions and attempts to circumvent Jibly’s fees or Platform rules.

Jibly may use automated tools to support functions such as matching, security, fraud detection, identity verification status, payment administration and other Platform operations. We do not currently rely solely on automated decision-making that produces legal or similarly significant effects on Users.

We may also use personal data for another purpose where that purpose is compatible with the reason the information was originally collected. Where applicable law requires a different lawful basis, additional notice or consent for a materially different use, we will take the steps required before carrying out that processing.
We do not use personal data for purposes that are incompatible with those described in this Privacy Policy unless the processing is otherwise permitted or required by applicable law.
RETENTION AND DELETION

Jibly keeps personal data only for as long as reasonably necessary for the purposes for which it was collected and processed. Different categories of information are therefore retained for different periods.

Unless a longer period is reasonably necessary because of an active dispute, chargeback, investigation, legal claim, regulatory request or other legal requirement, Jibly generally applies the following retention periods:

Account and profile information: retained while the Account remains active. Following Account closure or deletion, information that is no longer required will normally be deleted or anonymised within 30 days, subject to the limited fraud-prevention record described below.

Fraud-prevention record following Account closure: Jibly may retain a restricted record containing the User’s name, email address, telephone number and relevant payment or Stripe reference information for up to five years after Account closure where reasonably necessary to detect or prevent fraud, repeated misuse, circumvention of suspension or termination, or attempts by a restricted User to create a new Account. This information will be used only for those purposes, access will be restricted, and the record will be automatically deleted at the end of the retention period unless further retention is required or permitted by law.
Booking and transaction records: retained for six years after completion or cancellation of the relevant Booking.
Payment, refund, Payout and chargeback records: retained for six years after the relevant transaction is completed or the matter is finally resolved.
Platform messages connected with a Booking: normally retained for two years after the Booking is completed or cancelled.

Handover and delivery records: Handover Codes, Delivery Codes, delivery photographs, parcel photographs, inspection confirmations and other evidence relating to collection or delivery are normally retained for two years after completion or cancellation of the relevant Booking.

Stored files: where photographs, delivery evidence or other files are stored separately from Jibly’s main database, those stored files will be deleted when the corresponding retention period expires. Deleting or anonymising the associated database record does not mean that Jibly will intentionally retain the separate stored file beyond the applicable retention period.
Support enquiries and ordinary complaints: normally retained for two years after the matter has been closed.

Disputes, chargebacks, investigations and legal claims: where a Booking, communication, photograph, transaction record or other information is relevant to an active or reasonably anticipated dispute, chargeback, investigation or legal claim, Jibly may suspend the ordinary deletion period and retain the relevant information until the matter has been finally resolved and, where reasonably necessary for the establishment, exercise or defence of legal claims, for up to six years after resolution.

Fraud, security and Account-enforcement records: normally retained for two years after the relevant incident or Account action, except for the limited five-year fraud-prevention record described above or where longer retention is reasonably necessary because of repeated fraud, an investigation, legal proceedings or a regulatory requirement.

Identity verification information held by Jibly: Jibly does not ordinarily retain copies of the underlying identity documents, selfies or verification images submitted to Stripe. Jibly may retain verification status, dates, reference identifiers and related records while the Account remains active and normally for two years after Account closure, unless the information forms part of a Booking, dispute, fraud investigation, legal claim or other matter requiring longer retention.

Reviews: reviews may remain available for as long as they remain relevant to the integrity and operation of the marketplace. Where an Account is deleted, Jibly may retain the review in anonymised or de-identified form so that it no longer directly identifies the former User.

Technical and security logs: retention of certain infrastructure, hosting and database logs may be determined by the relevant service provider rather than Jibly. Those providers may retain logs in accordance with their own retention periods and privacy practices. Where Jibly separately controls technical or security logs, they will be retained only for as long as reasonably necessary for security, fraud prevention, troubleshooting or legal purposes.
Where the same information falls within more than one category, Jibly may apply the longest retention period that remains reasonably necessary for a legitimate purpose.
At the end of the applicable retention period, personal data will be deleted, securely put beyond use or anonymised unless further retention is permitted or required by applicable law.

Jibly periodically reviews its retention practices and may shorten a retention period where information is no longer reasonably required. Personal data will not be kept indefinitely merely because it may potentially be useful in the future.

Information processed independently by third-party providers, including Stripe, may be retained by those providers in accordance with their own legal obligations, retention periods and privacy policies.
INFORMATION SHARING

We may share personal data where reasonably necessary to operate the Platform, provide Jibly’s services, process transactions, protect Users, comply with law or administer our business. This may include sharing information with:
Other Users

, where necessary to facilitate a Trip, Item Request, Booking, handover, delivery or communication between the parties. We only make information available to other Users where it is relevant to the marketplace interaction or Platform feature involved.
Stripe and payment or identity-verification providers

, for payment processing, payouts, refunds, chargebacks, identity verification, fraud prevention and related transaction or compliance purposes. These providers may process certain information under their own privacy notices and legal obligations.
Technology and service providers

, including providers that support hosting, databases, authentication, email delivery, communications, security, analytics, customer support and other technical functions required to operate Jibly. This currently includes providers such as Supabase, Vercel, Resend and Zoho.
Professional advisers and business service providers
, including lawyers, accountants, auditors, insurers and other advisers where access to information is reasonably necessary for them to provide services to Jibly.
Authorities, courts and regulators
, where disclosure is required by law, court order, regulatory requirement or lawful request, or where reasonably necessary to establish, exercise or defend legal rights.
Fraud, safety and enforcement recipients
, where reasonably necessary to investigate suspected fraud, security incidents, prohibited conduct, threats to safety, misuse of the Platform or breaches of the Marketplace Terms.
Corporate transaction parties

, where Jibly is involved in a merger, acquisition, financing, restructuring, sale of assets or similar corporate transaction. Information may be disclosed to relevant advisers, potential counterparties or successor entities subject to appropriate confidentiality and data-protection safeguards.
We may also share information where you specifically ask us to do so, where you give valid consent, or where disclosure is otherwise permitted by applicable data protection law.
We do not sell personal data to third parties. We also do not disclose personal data to third parties for their own unrelated marketing purposes without an appropriate lawful basis.

Where a service provider processes personal data on Jibly’s behalf, we require appropriate contractual and security protections where required by law. Where a third party determines its own purposes and means of processing, its handling of personal data may instead be governed by its own privacy notice.
INTERNATIONAL DATA TRANSFER

Jibly is based in the United Kingdom, but some of the service providers we use, and some Users or recipients of personal data, may be located outside the United Kingdom or the European Economic Area. This means personal data may be transferred to, accessed from or stored in countries that may have different data protection laws.

Where Jibly transfers personal data internationally, we will use an appropriate transfer mechanism where required by applicable law. This may include transferring data to a country recognised as providing an adequate level of protection, relying on approved contractual safeguards such as the UK International Data Transfer Agreement or Addendum, or using another lawful transfer mechanism available under applicable data protection law.

Where appropriate, we may also carry out transfer risk assessments and implement additional technical, contractual or organisational safeguards to protect personal data during an international transfer.

Some third-party providers, including Stripe and other technology providers, may process personal data in multiple countries as part of their global operations. Their processing and international transfers may also be governed by their own privacy notices, contractual safeguards and legal obligations.

Where a Booking is made with WEF Technologies FZE LLC in the United Arab Emirates, Jibly Limited shares with it the personal data needed to handle that Booking, its Payment and its Payout: the Booking details, and the names, contact details, identity verification status and payout status of the Sender and the Traveller on that Booking. The United Arab Emirates is not recognised as providing an adequate level of protection under UK data protection law, so these transfers are made only under the UK International Data Transfer Agreement or another approved safeguard in place between the two companies.
You may contact us at contact@jibly.io if you would like further information about the safeguards used for a particular international transfer.
DATA STORAGE AND SECURITY

Jibly stores personal data using third-party technology and hosting providers that support the operation of the Platform. This currently includes services such as Supabase for database infrastructure and Vercel for web hosting. Depending on the provider and service involved, personal data may be stored or processed in the United Kingdom, the European Economic Area or other countries in accordance with the international transfer safeguards described in this Privacy Policy.

We use reasonable and appropriate technical and organisational measures designed to protect personal data against accidental or unlawful destruction, loss, alteration, unauthorised disclosure or access. These measures may include access controls, authentication measures, encryption where appropriate, secure hosting arrangements, logging, monitoring, restricted internal access and other security controls appropriate to the nature of the information and the risks involved.

Access to personal data is limited to persons and service providers who reasonably need it for the purposes described in this Privacy Policy. Where third-party providers process personal data on Jibly’s behalf, we require appropriate data protection and security arrangements where required by law.

No website, online service, database or method of electronic transmission can be guaranteed to be completely secure. Although Jibly takes reasonable steps to protect personal data, we cannot guarantee absolute security against every possible cyberattack, system failure, unauthorised access or other security incident.

Users are also responsible for helping protect their Accounts, including by keeping login credentials confidential, using appropriate passwords and notifying Jibly promptly if they believe their Account or personal information has been compromised.

If Jibly becomes aware of a personal data breach, we will assess the incident and take appropriate steps in accordance with applicable data protection law, including notifying affected individuals or the relevant supervisory authority where legally required.
COOKIES AND SIMILAR TECHNOLOGIES

Jibly currently uses only cookies and similar technologies that are strictly necessary for the operation of the Platform, including maintaining User sessions and saving draft form information. These technologies are used to provide functionality requested by the User and to maintain the operation and security of the Platform. Jibly does not currently use analytics cookies, advertising cookies or third-party tracking technologies. As Jibly currently uses only strictly necessary technologies, it does not currently display a cookie-consent banner for those technologies. If Jibly introduces non-essential cookies or similar technologies in the future, this Privacy Policy and the Platform’s consent arrangements will be updated as required by applicable law.
THIRD-PARTY LINKS

The Platform may contain links to websites, services or content operated by third parties. Jibly does not control those third parties and is not responsible for their privacy practices, content or security. If you follow a third-party link or use a third-party service, any personal data you provide will be handled in accordance with that third party’s own terms and privacy policy, and you should review those documents before providing personal information.

Depending on the applicable law, you may have one or more of the following rights in respect of your personal information:

Right of Access: You may have the right to ask whether we process personal information about you and, where we do, to receive a copy of that information together with information about how it is being used.
Right to Rectification: You may have the right to ask us to correct personal information that is inaccurate and to complete information that is incomplete.

Right to Erasure: In certain circumstances, you may have the right to ask us to delete your personal information. This right is not absolute. For example, we may need to retain information where it is required to comply with a legal obligation or where it is necessary to establish, exercise or defend a legal claim.

Right to Restrict Processing: Where UK or EU/EEA data protection law applies, you may have the right to ask us to restrict how we use your personal information in certain circumstances, including while we consider a challenge concerning the accuracy of the information or an objection to our processing.

Right to Object: Where we process your personal information on the basis of legitimate interests, you may have the right to object to that processing because of your particular circumstances. If personal information is used for direct marketing, you may object to that use at any time.

Right to Data Portability: Where UK or EU/EEA data protection law applies, you may have the right to receive certain personal information that you provided to us in a structured, commonly used and machine-readable format and, where technically feasible, ask for it to be transferred to another controller. This right generally applies where the information is processed by automated means and the processing is based on your consent or a contract with you.

Right to Withdraw Consent: Where we rely on your consent to process personal information, you may withdraw that consent at any time. Withdrawing consent does not affect any processing that was lawfully carried out before you withdrew it.

Rights Relating to Automated Decisions: Where applicable law gives you rights in relation to decisions made solely by automated means that produce legal or similarly significant effects, you may exercise those rights in the circumstances provided by law. Jibly does not currently rely solely on automated decision-making that produces legal or similarly significant effects on Users.

Rights Under Swiss Law: If the Swiss Federal Act on Data Protection applies to our processing of your personal information, you may have rights including the right to obtain information about whether and how your personal information is processed, to request correction of inaccurate information and, where the applicable requirements are met, to request deletion or destruction of personal information. Swiss law also provides protections concerning certain automated individual decisions.
Making a Request

To exercise a data protection right, please contact us at contact@jibly.io and tell us what you would like us to do. We may ask you for information reasonably necessary to confirm your identity before acting on your request, particularly where a request involves access to or deletion of personal information.

We will normally respond to requests made under the UK GDPR within one month. Where permitted by applicable law, this period may be extended where a request is particularly complex or where we have received a number of requests. If we need more time, we will tell you and explain the reason for the extension.

There is normally no charge for exercising your data protection rights. However, where permitted by applicable law, we may charge a reasonable fee or refuse to act on a request that is manifestly unfounded or excessive. Any decision to do so will be considered on the circumstances of the particular request.

Some data protection rights are subject to conditions and exceptions. We may therefore be unable to comply with all or part of a request where applicable law allows or requires us to retain or continue processing the relevant information, including for legal, tax, accounting, fraud-prevention or legal-claims purposes.
Complaints
If you have concerns about how we process your personal information, you can contact us first at contact@jibly.io, and we will try to address the issue.
If you are in the United Kingdom, you have the right to complain to the Information Commissioner's Office (ICO).

If EU or EEA data protection law applies to you, you may have the right to complain to the competent data protection supervisory authority, including the supervisory authority in the country where you live or work or where you believe a breach of data protection law occurred.
If Swiss data protection law applies to you, you may contact the Federal Data Protection and Information Commissioner (FDPIC) about concerns relating to the processing of your personal information.
You do not have to contact us before exercising any right to complain directly to a supervisory authority where applicable law gives you that right.
